hints: The answers compare hidden values at two indices.
Sort indices with an interactive comparison-based sort.
The position of an index in sorted order is its hidden value.
analogy: Sort labeled boxes by their hidden contents; because contents are 1 through n, each box's rank reveals its number.
example: If sorted indices are [2,3,1], their values are 1,2,3, so the permutation is [3,1,2].
algorithm: Read n and merge-sort indices using queries ? i j to compare hidden values. Flush every question and read YES or NO before continuing. Assign value r to the index at sorted rank r; print the completed permutation after !, flush, and terminate.
correctness: The judge supplies the true strict order and all hidden values are distinct. Sorting recovers their exact order, and the value at rank r must be r because the values form a permutation of 1 through n.
complexity: For n<=1000, merge sort uses at most n*ceil(log2 n)-2^ceil(log2 n)+1 <= 8977 queries, within 10000, and O(n) space.
